text:
support-oncall: Heads up — since 03:10 UTC yesterday we've seen a spike in customer tickets (502/504 on /v1/generate, intermittent invalid_signature errors, elevated p95 latency). ~120 customer-facing tickets so far. Tickets reference a KMS rotation that ran at 03:09. Filing here to see if this ties to the pen-test finding about KMS alias enumeration.
alex: Acknowledged. Can you paste one of the recent sample request failures and the relevant CloudTrail event IDs? Also which key was rotated? @maria FYI for infra impact.
support-oncall: Sample error from customer A:

```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-request-id: r-92f7a
x-upstream: gateway-timeout
body: {"error":"invalid_signature","message":"signature does not match"}
```

CloudTrail payloads: ct-evt-20260315-9876, ct-evt-20260315-9881
Rotated key alias: alias/redwood-inference-prod-model-keys (rotation job id rot-20260315-03)

priya: From the pentest side — we flagged alias enumeration via ListAliases in a non-prod account earlier, which could expose key naming patterns. We marked it medium because it requires credentials to enumerate. I ran a quick retest in staging and couldn't reproduce with current policies.
maria: Correlating: rotation job touched key metadata and triggered a short HSM soft-fail fallback in the rotation-helper, causing retries in the auth path. That aligns with 502/504 and latency spikes. Not seeing direct exploit evidence yet.
james: We also see billing gaps — some customers received duplicate billing events for token usage between 03:10–03:18 (likely retries). Need to reconcile with finance.
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-142. Assigned to eng-sre and sec oncall. Priority: P2 (pending triage).

alex: Priya, given pen-test context, does the alias enumeration change exploitability here? If an attacker enumerated aliases, could they cause the rotation job to leak or trigger fallback behavior? Any chain to service disruption?

priya: Unclear. Enumeration by itself doesn't cause rotation errors. But if an attacker had credentials to call KMS or trigger rotation jobs (e.g., via compromised pipeline), they could induce edge cases. For now: exploitability low without further creds. Evidence: staging retest logs attached to report (can't paste here) show ListAliases returns names but no key material. Severity remains medium on the report side due to information disclosure.

maria: Customer impact is high regardless — production latency and billing noise. Suggest we treat this as two tracks:
1) Operational mitigation (P0): rollback last rotation, disable rotation-helper for that key, increase auth retry jitter, patch fallback path.
2) Security validation (P1): reproduce pen-test chain with least-priv privilege account, confirm whether alias enumeration can be combined with rotation-trigger calls.

alex: Agreed. Owners:
- rollback/mitigation: @maria (eng-sre) + @james (infra)
- sec repro & retest: @priya (pen-test) + @alex (sec lead)
- customer comms & billing reconciliation: @support-oncall + @finance (cc)

maria: I'll open a rollback runbook now. Rolling back to pre-03:09 key config in 20m unless there are objections. We'll put a maintenance banner and notify impacted customers.

support-oncall: Please also include a snippet for reproducing the auth error — ops asked for a minimal curl to test. Proposed repro:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/open-7b","input":"ping"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Look for 502 + x-request-id matching CloudTrail event.

priya: I'll attempt the chained repro in a controlled repro account: steps:
- list aliases with least-priv creds
- trigger rotation-helper via api (simulate rotation event)
- monitor CloudTrail & KMS logs for Get/Decrypt errors

If I can produce a path that both enumerates and triggers fallback, we escalate severity.

james: FYI logs show repeated KMS response code 503 around 03:11 on a subset of HSMs. Might be a partial outage. We'll throttle rotation jobs and add a circuit breaker to rotation-helper.

alex: Good. Decision: treat immediate customer impact as P0 and proceed with rollback + mitigation. Security team will continue retest and update the pen-test finding severity if we find an exploit chain. Keep this thread updated with artifacts (CloudTrail ids, x-req ids, repro results). :thumbsup:

maria: Rollback started at 03:42 UTC. ETA 12m. Will post status.

support-oncall: Posted a brief customer status note and informed support queue. Thanks.

priya: Running controlled repro now. Will post logs + verdict here once complete.

sec-bot: INC-20260315-142 status update: mitigation in progress. Next update in 15m.
